children.name: Sagittarius
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the singular secretarybird, a distinctive raptor of African savannas that hunts almost entirely on foot. Standing over a metre tall on long, crane-like legs, it is equally at home stalking through tall grass or soaring on thermals, and its unique morphology places it in its own family within Accipitriformes.

children.name: Sagittarius serpentarius
children.description:
The secretarybird or secretary bird (Sagittarius serpentarius) is a large bird of prey that is endemic to Africa. It is mostly terrestrial, spending most of its time on the ground, and is usually found in the open grasslands and savanna of the sub-Saharan region. John Frederick Miller described the species in 1779. A member of the order Accipitriformes, which also includes many other diurnal birds of prey such as eagles, hawks, kites, vultures, and harriers, it is placed in its own family, the Sagittariidae.
The secretarybird is instantly recognizable as a very large bird with an eagle-like body on crane-like legs that give the bird a height of as much as. The sexes are similar in appearance. Adults have a featherless, red-orange face and predominantly grey plumage, with a flattened dark crest and black flight feathers and thighs.
